names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 28 Οκτωβρίου, «Άγιος Κυριάκος ο Ιερομάρτυρας», with the rank words left off. The page glosses the name from κύριος, the one dedicated to the Lord.

Read out of the title on his name link behind the line for 28 октября ст. ст., «Святитель Кириак Иерусалимский, патриарх, сщмч.», with the rank words and the grade left off. The line itself declines the name and spells the see out in Russian rather than as a by-name.

death.note: Two calendars, two years, and neither is preferred. saint.gr: «Όταν το 361 μ.Χ. ο Ιουλιανός ο Παραβάτης εκστράτευσε κατά των Περσών και πέρασε από την Ιερουσαλήμ, έμαθε για τον Κυριάκο…» — its year for Julian's passage through Jerusalem, with the arrest, the torments and the death following in the same notice and no further date. days.pravoslavie.ru's line for 28 октября ст. ст. prints «(363)» after his name, which is the year Julian died in Persia. The interval is the union of the two.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 28 октября ст. ст. — «Сщмч. Кириака , Патриарха Иерусалимского (363).»
source.note: The line stands in the day's second paragraph, which carries no typikon icon, so no rank is recorded.

attestations.note: The Russian agrees with the Greek day this folder was written from and with its reading of the man — a bishop of Jerusalem killed under Julian — **but not with its year**: the Greek page dates him 361, from Julian's passage through Jerusalem, and this line prints «(363)», the year of that emperor's death on the Persian campaign. Neither is preferred and the interval now carries both. The Russian also calls the see a patriarchate where the Greek calls it a bishopric; the folder's `office` is left as it was. No life page follows his name; his name page carries three icons, this day alone, and no text.
Not checked: doxologia.ro's calendar for the same civil day (1 October 2026).

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 28ης Οκτωβρίου — «Άγιος Κυριάκος ο Ιερομάρτυρας»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 28 Οκτωβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. The man is identified by what the page says of him and not by his name: he showed the Precious Cross to Saint Helen and was afterwards bishop of Jerusalem, and he suffered under Julian the Apostate in 361. The corpus keeps eleven other Cyriacuses and none of them is a bishop of Jerusalem, and no folder held an office of Jerusalem of that name before this one. His mother Anna is kept on the same day and is a folder of this batch. No hymn. No asterisk and not the sentence «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη η ύπαρξη του Αγίου».
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue as printed by pravoslavno.rs (1 October 2026).
